import itertools, random
n=12
fixed={(0,9),(1,10),(2,9)}
r=[3]*n
for u,v in fixed:
    r[u]-=1; r[v]-=1
print(r, sum(r))
# backtracking choose vertex max residual
def search(r, edges):
    if sum(r)==0: return edges
    # fail if any neg or degree too high
    if any(x<0 for x in r): return None
    # choose vertex with max r
    # pruning: each vertex has enough candidates with residual
    for i,ri in enumerate(r):
        if ri>0:
            cnt=sum(1 for j in range(n) if j!=i and r[j]>0 and tuple(sorted((i,j))) not in fixed and tuple(sorted((i,j))) not in edges)
            if cnt<ri: return None
    v=max(range(n), key=lambda i:r[i])
    d=r[v]
    # candidates with positive residual not forbidden or existing
    c=[u for u in range(n) if u!=v and r[u]>0 and tuple(sorted((u,v))) not in fixed and tuple(sorted((u,v))) not in edges]
    # try combos of d neighbors; order heuristic high degree
    c=sorted(c, key=lambda u:-r[u])
    for neigh in itertools.combinations(c,d):
        # possible: no duplicate among combo irrelevant
        nr=r[:]
        nr[v]=0
        nedges=set(edges)
        ok=True
        for u in neigh:
            nr[u]-=1
            if nr[u]<0: ok=False; break
            nedges.add(tuple(sorted((u,v))))
        if not ok: continue
        # Erdos-Gallai? skip
        res=search(nr,nedges)
        if res is not None: return res
    return None
